vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-399: Release specialist — coordinated post-merge rollout and release safety

plan.title: Release specialist — coordinated post-merge rollout and release safety
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: A cross-repo/multi-service change can merge cleanly yet leave production unusable if components roll out in the wrong order or a later deploy fails after an earlier one succeeded. PAN-632 owns coordinated merge and emits a merged change-set manifest (the MergeSet in src/lib/merge-set.ts). Nothing today owns coordinated release: there is no releaseStatus, no release: config, and no rollout ordering / health-check / rollback machinery.
narratives.Proposal: Add a deterministic release specialist that runs inside postMergeLifecycle (src/lib/cloister/merge-agent.ts:319) after the issue reaches verifying_on_main. It reads the merged MergeSet, loads the project's release: config, resolves an ordered component plan (topological sort over depends_on, excluding trigger:skip), then for each component in order honors the trigger mode, polls health_url for auto components, runs version_check and smoke_test, halts remaining components on failure, and runs the rollback hook where configured. Per-component state persists to a new release set (mirroring the merge set); issue-level releaseStatus (pending->releasing->passed|failed|partial|rolled_back|skipped) is written through the existing setReviewStatusSync write door and surfaced on the dashboard. Projects with no release: config are skipped cleanly.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Actively invoking provider deploy commands for auto components (kubectl apply, vercel deploy); MVP waits for external auto-deploy and verifies via health_url/version_check/smoke_test.
- Filtering the release plan to only the change-set's affected components (needs a repo->component mapping that does not exist yet); MVP releases the full ordered project component graph.
- Gating pan close / issue completion on releaseStatus; surfacing partial/failed/rolled_back is sufficient for MVP.
- Pre-merge review/test coordination, PR/MR creation, rebasing, or conflict resolution (owned by PAN-632 and the merge pipeline).
- A generic provider-plugin abstraction; the provider field is informational metadata for now.

autoDecisions.rationale: The issue lists Kubernetes/Vercel as trigger:auto; their CI already deploys. The specialist polls health_url and runs version_check/smoke_test rather than shelling out to kubectl/vercel. Actively triggering provider deploys is a larger provider-specific effort out of scope for the first cut.

autoDecisions.summary: Release set mirrors the merge set (release_sets/release_set_components + ReleaseSet model)
autoDecisions.rationale: Reuses the established per-issue/per-component persistence and model shape from src/lib/merge-set.ts rather than inventing a new pattern; convention-aligned and dashboard-ready.

autoDecisions.summary: CLI verb is `pan rollout`, not `pan release`
autoDecisions.rationale: `pan release` already exists as the npm stable/canary publish flow (src/cli/commands/release.ts). Overloading it is confusing and lint-fragile. Config key stays release: and status stays releaseStatus per the issue.

autoDecisions.summary: MYN AC verified by resolver fixture test + docs, not by editing live projects.yaml
autoDecisions.rationale: projects.yaml is machine config under ~/.overdeck/ outside the repo. AC2 is proven by a topo-sort test over a MYN-shaped fixture (frontend depends_on api; docs: skip) plus the documented example.

autoDecisions.summary: Close-out is NOT gated on releaseStatus in MVP
autoDecisions.rationale: Surfacing partial/failed/rolled_back state meets the 6 acceptance criteria; auto-blocking pan close on release state is a scoped follow-up and avoids touching the close-out flow now.

autoDecisions.summary: MVP releases the full ordered project component graph, not only affected components
autoDecisions.rationale: Filtering to affected components requires a repo->component mapping that does not exist; releasing the full ordered graph is safe for idempotent auto-deploys plus health checks and meets AC2.

items.title: Add release: config schema to ProjectConfig with parsing and a test

This is the public config contract that the engine, resolver, and docs depend on — name fields exactly as in the issue's YAML example.

Add ReleaseSet model and release-set-db CRUD mirroring merge-set

Mirror the JSON fallback in review-status-json.ts. Do NOT change readyForMerge derivation (release is post-merge).

items.title: setReviewStatusSync(issueId, { releaseStatus: 'releasing' }) then getReviewStatusSync returns releaseStatus === 'releasing'
Setting releaseStatus records a status_history row of type 'release' with that status
Writing releaseStatus preserves the existing reviewStatus, testStatus, mergeStatus, and readyForMerge on the same row
Expose releaseStatus in the per-issue permanent pipeline record

narrative.Action: In src/lib/pan-dir/records.ts, add `releaseStatus: status?.releaseStatus ?? 'pending'` to the pipeline block built in buildIssueRecord (near line 95-100 alongside mergeStatus/readyForMerge). Ensure the ProjectPipeline record type includes releaseStatus.

items.title: buildIssueRecord emits pipeline.releaseStatus reflecting the stored review-status releaseStatus, defaulting to 'pending' when unset
A record round-trips releaseStatus through the .pan/records/<issue>.json pipeline block without dropping it
Resolve an ordered release plan by topological sort over depends_on

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/release/release-plan.ts exporting a pure resolveReleasePlan(release: ReleaseConfig): ReleaseComponentPlanEntry[] that: excludes components with trigger:'skip'; topologically sorts the remainder by depends_on so a component always follows its dependencies; assigns a stable releaseOrder integer; and throws a clear Error naming the cycle when depends_on contains a cycle. depends_on entries pointing at a skipped/absent component are treated as satisfied (with a note) rather than fataling.

items.title: Given MYN-shaped config (frontend depends_on [api], docs skip), resolveReleasePlan returns [api, frontend] in that order and omits docs
Given a depends_on cycle (a->b->a), resolveReleasePlan throws an Error whose message names the cycle members
resolveReleasePlan returns entries whose releaseOrder places each component strictly after all of its depends_on components
Run the ordered release with health/version/smoke checks, stop-on-failure, and rollback

metadata.readinessReason: Confined to the new src/lib/release/release-engine.ts plus its own test; depends only on the already-landed config/model/resolver items (blocks edges enforce that ordering) and shares no files with siblings, so it is parallel-safe once its dependencies land.

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/release/release-engine.ts exporting runRelease(issueId, projectPath). It: reads the merged MergeSet via getMergeSetSync(issueId) as the trigger input; loads the project release config; calls resolveReleasePlan; builds+persists a ReleaseSet; sets issue releaseStatus='releasing'. For each component in order: trigger:'manual' -> mark component 'blocked' (awaiting manual deploy), continue without failing the release; trigger:'auto' -> poll health_url until a healthy response or a bounded timeout, then run version_check then smoke_test when configured. On any stage failure: mark the component 'failed', HALT all remaining components, run rollback (async) if configured (component -> 'rolled_back'), and set issue releaseStatus to 'rolled_back' if any rollback ran else 'failed'; if some required components passed and a later one failed, use 'partial' per spec. All shell runs via async exec/spawn with explicit timeouts (NEVER execSync). Persist per-component state transitions through the release-set model. On all-pass, set releaseStatus='passed'. Injectable clock/exec seam so tests use fake timers.

items.title: Given all components healthy and smoke_test exit 0, runRelease sets each component 'passed' and issue releaseStatus 'passed'
When an earlier component passes and a later component's smoke_test fails, runRelease halts remaining components and sets issue releaseStatus to 'failed' or 'partial' (never 'passed')
When a component fails and has a rollback command, runRelease executes it, marks that component 'rolled_back', and sets issue releaseStatus 'rolled_back'
All health/version/smoke/rollback execution goes through async exec/spawn with a timeout; the module contains no execSync call
Trigger the release specialist from postMergeLifecycle after verifying_on_main

narrative.Action: In src/lib/cloister/merge-agent.ts postMergeLifecycle, after transitionIssueToVerifyingOnMain succeeds (~line 451, fresh-process path), invoke the release specialist: if the project has a release: config, call runRelease(issueId, projectPath) (awaited or fire-and-tracked so a slow release does not block the lifecycle return); if no release: config, skip cleanly (set releaseStatus 'skipped' or leave unset — no failure). Keep the step idempotent and inside the existing in-flight/_completedPostMerge guards so re-entry does not double-run a release. Do not weaken the in-flight guard.

items.title: Given a project with a release: config, postMergeLifecycle runs runRelease exactly once and updates the issue releaseStatus off 'pending'
Given a project without a release: config, postMergeLifecycle marks releaseStatus 'skipped' (or leaves it unset) and never sets a failing value — runRelease is not called
Given an already-released issue, re-entering postMergeLifecycle refuses to run runRelease a second time and in-flight-guard.test.ts passes
Surface release status and component-level failure context on the dashboard

narrative.Action: Thread releaseStatus (already on ReviewStatusSnapshot) and the per-component release-set state into a dashboard read surface so an operator sees issue-level release status and which component failed. Add a release row/section to the review-pipeline overview (ReviewPipelineSection or the issue header) rendering releaseStatus and, on failure, the failing component key + notes. Follow pan-style-guide: muted status text, no pill badges, no decorative color; red reserved for genuine failure. Confirm the exact server read surface that assembles ReviewStatusSnapshot for the frontend before wiring (files_scope_confidence low).

items.title: When an issue has releaseStatus 'releasing', the review-pipeline section renders a release indicator showing that state
When releaseStatus is 'failed'/'partial'/'rolled_back', the UI renders the failing component key and its notes
When an issue has no release activity (releaseStatus 'pending'/'skipped'/unset), no release indicator clutters the row
Add pan rollout status/retry CLI plus its skill wrapper

narrative.Action: Add a new commander verb `pan rollout` (registered in src/cli/index.ts) with subcommands `status <id>` (prints the release set: releaseStatus + per-component status/order) and `retry <id>` (re-runs runRelease for the issue). Named `rollout` to avoid colliding with the existing `pan release` npm-publish verb. Create skills/pan-rollout/SKILL.md documenting exactly the flags/subcommands so scripts/lint-skills.sh passes (skills<->CLI lockstep).

items.title: `pan rollout status <id>` prints the issue's releaseStatus and each component's key, order, and status
`pan rollout retry <id>` runs runRelease again for the issue and prints the resulting releaseStatus
npm run lint passes: skills/pan-rollout/SKILL.md documents every subcommand and flag that `pan rollout --help` emits (lint-skills.sh finds no drift)
Integration tests: ordering, stop-on-failure, rollback, skip-clean (fake timers)

expected_outputs: release-integration.test.ts passes with fake timers (no real waits)

narrative.Action: Add an integration test exercising runRelease end-to-end against fixtures with injected exec results: (1) full-pass ordered release; (2) mid-plan failure halts remaining and yields failed/partial; (3) failure with rollback yields rolled_back; (4) no release: config -> skipped cleanly, engine not run. All health-poll/timeout waits driven by vi.useFakeTimers() + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(); no real setTimeout waits, no maxForks:1.

items.title: The ordering test asserts components execute in resolved depends_on order and passes using only advanceTimersByTimeAsync (no real delay)
The stop-on-failure test passes and shows no component after the failed one runs (the later components' exec mock receives no call)
The skip-clean test asserts a project without release: config produces no releaseStatus failure and does not invoke exec
Document the release: config section and MYN example

expected_outputs: docs contain a release: block matching the parsed schema and MYN example

narrative.Action: Add a Release Configuration section to configuration/projects.mdx documenting the release: schema (components, provider, trigger auto|manual|skip, depends_on, health_url, version_check, smoke_test, rollback), the releaseStatus lifecycle, the wait-and-verify semantics for trigger:auto, the skip-clean behavior for projects without release:, and the full MYN example from the issue. Note that the CLI verb is `pan rollout` (distinct from the npm-publish `pan release`).

items.title: configuration/projects.mdx contains a release: example whose component fields exactly match the ReleaseComponentConfig type (provider, trigger, depends_on, health_url, version_check, smoke_test, rollback)

configuration/projects.mdx contains a list enumerating all seven releaseStatus values (pending, releasing, passed, failed, partial, rolled_back, skipped) and a sentence that states projects without a release: section are skipped cleanly
